LootPlot promised a simple yet engaging premise: strategically acquire items, and watch your score soar. Initially, it delivered. There was a satisfying loop of finding new loot, making smart purchasing decisions, and feeling the progression as your score climbed higher and higher. It was the kind of game you could pick up for a few minutes or lose an hour to, always feeling like you were making progress. However, over time, the developer's updates seemed to actively dismantle what made the game enjoyable. Each patch felt less like an improvement and more like a step backward. Core mechanics that once provided a sense of accomplishment were tweaked, diluted. The balance shifted dramatically, making it harder to feel the same sense of progression or the thrill of a good loot drop. What was once a fun, addictive experience slowly devolved into a frustrating grind. The very "fun" the game offered was systematically stripped away, leaving behind a hollow shell of its former self. It's a shame to see a game with such a promising start go down this path, ultimately becoming something I can no longer recommend.

This game has a lot of interesting mechanics and really tries and succeeds at giving the player significant agency in interacting with the mechanics and setting the mechanics up to interact with each other and normally I would very much recommend the game, however the tile mechanic allows for soft locks to occur very easily. In fact the interactions that can cause this are directly intended to be able to do as such by the developer. This is incredibly frustrating. I am all for a game like this giving you a ton of control such as giving you RNG choices that could tank a good run, those things feels entertaining and you have the opportunity to watch as your build crumbles, but with a soft lock it makes the entire run leading up to that point feel like a complete waste of time and you have literally zero other option than going to main menu and starting a new run. As a player that is so incredibly unsatisfying. I have over a thousand hours in the binding of Isaac and there have been hundreds of runs where a run is ruined by one bad choice but the game does everything possible to never soft lock you so I have no issue with playing out a bad run end, being punished for the choice, and starting over, but for a game where the design is specifically intended to allow you to just be stuck it makes me want to never play the game again even if the execution is otherwise very impressive for such a complex concept.

if you've played balatro for more than a few hours you've probably realized that the poker element is basically a red herring and 99.9% of the game is acquiring jokers and putting them in the right order. in a lot of the strongest builds your poker hand doesn't matter at all, you just play any card and get a billion points from your jokers. lootplot solved this issue by cutting out the middleman. arranging objects in space is the entire game it doesn't pretend to be about anything else. you have tiles, you have objects you put on the tiles. when you press the "pulse" button each tile activates in sequence. you can press the button six times in a level, and the goal is to get a certain score within those six presses. that's it. what really sets it apart from all the other engine-building games coming out right now is the extreme non-modality. everything in the game is on the same screen and functions the same way. there is no separate shop, instead there are "shop slots" which reset their item when pulsed. selling is the same way. slots can be created and modified anywhere on the board. you can activate items in the shop without buying them by placing something that activates other items in range. you can steal items by destroying the shop slot beneath them. you can add bonus points to the pulse button. you can accidentally destroy the pulse button and softlock the game. you can accidentally destroy the pulse button and use a reroll-based engine to win anyway. you can put a bowl in the wrong place and put yourself at negative a billion points. you can do anything.

虽然我仅仅过了一次教学角色，但我觉得现在我就能说，这是我玩过的最好玩的一款幸运房东类游戏（当然，还要算上大火的小丑牌类）。 其实因为随机性我算不上很喜欢这类型游戏，但是本作在该类型中真的是超级特质的一款： 非常烧脑，极少随机。 但是依旧保留了这类型的最大特征：爽快度拉满。 游戏中你获得的所有东西都会摆在你的场面上，没有任何随机抽牌要素。 几乎没有随机性的场面触发，虽然有点难想甚至到烧脑的程度，但是一旦成功构造出有趣结构后带来的爽快感，甚至远超大多同类游戏。 而且这游戏每一小阶段过后场面是保留的，这种不断扩建自己基地的感觉，在同类游戏中非常难得。 更棒的是，这游戏可以跳关。只要达到小阶段分数要求，觉得没什么好新增了后，就可以直接立即跳到下一关，大幅减少垃圾时间。 说完了我觉得棒的部分，提一点我觉得可以改进的。 首先，希望有个撤销功能。因为这游戏还挺费脑子的，有时候一下没想明白搞失误了，可能直接导致辛苦创建的帝国崩盘，挫折感拉满。为了防止撤销刷随机食物成功率，也可以让撤销后锁死随机数嘛。 然后，生成格子的道具效果说明里不解释格子有什么效果，让人摸不着头脑。还是应该额外出个框显示一下生成的格子的效果吧。有时候因为不知道格子效果甚至不敢选道具。 最后，像素游戏中文字体用这种书法体是怎么想的啊……真的难看，而且还有少数位置显示会重叠（某些食物的信息说明等）。能不能换个圆体或者黑体字体啊。
